headline: 29 dead as landslides strike Chittagong and Cox's Bazar
summary: Rain-triggered landslides have claimed 29 lives across the southeastern region, with train services between Chittagong and Cox's Bazar remaining suspended.
details: Landslides triggered by heavy rainfall have resulted in the deaths of 29 people across Chittagong and Cox's Bazar.
In Bandarban's Lama area, five people, including children, were killed when a hillside collapsed.
The disaster has severely impacted transportation, with train services on the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar route currently suspended.
Since July 5, at least 19 people have died and eight others were injured in similar rain-induced landslides in the region.
Rescue operations are ongoing as authorities work to manage the aftermath of the heavy rains and unstable terrain.
caption:
29 people killed in rain-triggered landslides across Chittagong and Cox's Bazar.

Landslides triggered by heavy rainfall have resulted in the deaths of 29 people across Chittagong and Cox's Bazar.

In Bandarban's Lama area, five people, including children, were killed when a hillside collapsed.

The disaster has severely impacted transportation, with train services on the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar route currently suspended.

Since July 5, at least 19 people have died and eight others were injured in similar rain-induced landslides in the region.

Rescue operations are ongoing as authorities work to manage the aftermath of the heavy rains and unstable terrain.

headline_marked: Dhaka says [[no lack of diplomatic efforts]] to bring back Sheikh Hasina
headline: Dhaka says no lack of diplomatic efforts to bring back Sheikh Hasina
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam says the government is pursuing prisoner exchange agreements to extradite the former PM.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that there is no lack of diplomatic efforts to bring former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh.
The Minister noted that Sheikh Hasina is currently abroad and is a convicted prisoner facing numerous allegations of oppression and crimes.
She emphasized that any statements made by the former Prime Minister are irrelevant to the legal process of her return.
The government aims to bring her back under the framework of prisoner exchange agreements.
Additionally, the State Minister mentioned that discussions between Dhaka and Delhi regarding the renewal of the Ganges Water Treaty, which expires in December, are progressing positively.
She also highlighted that professionalism is being prioritized in the appointment of new envoys to New York and Geneva, as well as new High Commissioners to Britain and India.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is currently undergoing reshuffles based on merit, skill, and professionalism as part of an ongoing process.
caption:
Dhaka is leaving no stone unturned to extradite Sheikh Hasina. The government is now eyeing prisoner exchange agreements to bring her back.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that there is no lack of diplomatic efforts to bring former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh.

The Minister noted that Sheikh Hasina is currently abroad and is a convicted prisoner facing numerous allegations of oppression and crimes.

She emphasized that any statements made by the former Prime Minister are irrelevant to the legal process of her return.

The government aims to bring her back under the framework of prisoner exchange agreements.

Additionally, the State Minister mentioned that discussions between Dhaka and Delhi regarding the renewal of the Ganges Water Treaty, which expires in December, are progressing positively.

She also highlighted that professionalism is being prioritized in the appointment of new envoys to New York and Geneva, as well as new High Commissioners to Britain and India.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is currently undergoing reshuffles based on merit, skill, and professionalism as part of an ongoing process.

#Bangladesh #SheikhHasina #Diplomacy #ForeignAffairs #Dhaka

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News
